column1: # The Stage 2 pair's undefended-branch ledger (#1408, parent #1401).
# Per function of bootstrap/stage2/compiler.c, how many of its branches
# nothing this repository runs ever takes -- once under each host compiler of
# the diverse pair. That set is where a divergence between compiler.kofun and
# its hand-maintained compiler.c transliteration can hide.
# A LISTED FUNCTION IS NOT WRONG. It is unwatched.
# AND A ROW IS NOT AUTOMATICALLY WORK. #1408 deliberately does not classify
# these as unreachable-by-construction versus reachable-but-uncovered --
# that judgement is per-region and belongs to the later children of #1401.
# This file is their work-list, so it has to say what a row does not mean.
# Some branches here cannot be reached by any fixture, because an earlier
# rule refuses first. The session working #1315 measured the shape: the
# `escaping store` and `escaping capture` reasons are unreachable, since
# Bytes is not an admitted record field type and cannot be captured, so
# E2S32 and E2S96 refuse before either is reached. They reported it rather
# than writing fixtures, because a fixture aimed there PASSES TODAY against
# a compiler that never implements the reason -- a defended-looking row
# defending nothing, which is worse than the undefended row it replaced.
# So: before writing a fixture to retire a row, check whether anything can
# reach it. A green fixture is not evidence that it could.
#   clang         clang version 22.1.8
#   basis         the union of the 172 driver rows and 1329 pinned *.kofun
#                 inputs that drivers.tsv and inputs.tsv held at that commit
#   totals        1987 untaken under gcc, 1892 under clang, across 370 functions
#   rows sha256   65a45f99e90e7ef7f1c665b366d4106d4541351cc8ea394d84cbbc6dfc8b3ffb
# WHAT MOVED, AND WHAT THIS MEASUREMENT CANNOT SAY ABOUT IT. The previous
# basis was 80e45fc7 (#1614, 2026-08-24). Between it and this one compiler.c
# changed five times: 7990f13c, 86908e4b, 6316f8ca and 63eea23f on 2026-09-06
# (#1540, #1581, #1515 and the record-edit diagnostics), none of which
# re-measured this file, and #1483's d1a9dc8f, which raised the lexical use
# budget from 256 to 4096 in build_scope_hir_mode and was measured twice. A
# single measurement over the whole span cannot attribute a row to one commit,
# so the split below is what the two #1483 runs isolate and no more. Two rows
# became fully covered, five entered, three changed count:
#   left:    hir_binding_declaration_start, lambda_binding_open
#            (both functions still exist; nothing untaken remains in them)
#   entered: move_positional_binding, move_positional_owner,
#            move_same_binding, move_straight_line_position,
#            validate_move_record_modes
#   changed: call_argument_parameter_property   gcc 13 -> 15, clang 11 -> 13
#            declared_bytes_argument_identity_error   gcc 9 -> 8, clang 8 -> 7
#            move_call_binding   clang 0 -> 1
# The five entered rows are the positional-move slice of #1540, the only one
# of those commits that introduced functions by these names; the three
# changed rows sit in the call-argument and Bytes-identity paths that
# 7990f13c and 86908e4b rewrote. That is an attribution by name, not by
# measurement, and the rows are the authority.
# NOT IN THIS BASIS: 63eea23f (#1515, PR #1640), merged at 14:27Z while this
# run was in progress and brought in under it by a merge commit rather than a
# rebase, so that the SHA above stays a real ancestor. It adds three C
# functions and four pinned inputs. #1640 said in as many words that whoever
# lands last regenerates this file; that is the run after this one, and it
# also owes mirror.tsv rows for those functions.
# What #1483 did to this ledger is measured exactly, because it ran twice.
# At 7beeebec, with the budget raised and nothing else, build_scope_hir_mode
# read 28 under both hosts against the 27 recorded here: the resolved-use
# refusal `use_count > 4096` had gone untaken. It had been covered by
# accident -- the pair's own bootstrap/stage2/compiler.kofun is a pinned
# corpus input and tripped that guard at line 906 on every run -- and the
# raised budget removed the accident. 78e75b41 adds a fixture that reaches
# it on purpose (tests/conformance/modules/lexical-scopes,
# `resolved-uses-4097`), and this run reads 27 again. Every other row is
# identical between the two #1483 runs, so the budget change itself moved
# nothing else.
# COST, measured on this run rather than estimated -- it is the number the
# `verify`-or-not argument in tooling/gate-reachability/unreachable.tsv rests
# on, and the reason that file rather than the verify list is where this gate
# is accounted for:
#   gcc    drivers  4663s + corpus 1530s =  103 min, drivers are 75% of it
#   clang  drivers  5060s + corpus 1609s =  111 min, drivers are 76% of it
#   both   drivers  9723s + corpus 3139s =  214 min for the pair
# THE CORPUS DOUBLED, AND ONE INPUT IS WHY. Against the previous run's 750s
# and 837s, the corpus phase is now 1530s and 1609s: compiler.kofun in `.c`
# mode ran 371s under the instrumented build when it refused at line 906 and
# runs about 1080s now that the whole scope-HIR stage precedes the
# `is_xid_start` refusal (#1513). measure.sh's per-input limit moved from
# 600s to 2400s for it, and tooling/machine-dependent/ledger.tsv records why.
# The first #1483 attempt timed that input out at 600s and this harness
# refused to report, as it is written to.
# READ THE PHASE SPLIT, NOT THE ABSOLUTE. These wall-clock figures are
# observations from one shared-machine run, not a clean-machine cost or a
# controlled cross-host comparison. No load sampler ran, so no same-contention
# claim is made or inferred from the two compiler timings.
# RETRIES. On each host `discovery` failed with exit=201 on all four attempts
# and is recorded as an expected failure in driver-failures.tsv, whose reason
# (the harness's instrumented compiler makes its two artifacts differ by
# construction) this run did not re-check. Neither host recorded a corpus
# timeout.
# DETERMINISM (#1408 criterion 5). This basis has one fresh two-compiler
# measurement: the run recorded above. The 7beeebec run is a different basis
# by one fixture and one driver and is cited only for the build_scope_hir_mode
# row it isolates; do not read it as a repeat of these rows.
# Regenerate with:
#   sh tests/pair-coverage/check.sh --count
# Regeneration is deliberately manual: the number moving is the event this
# file exists to make visible. `sh tests/pair-coverage/check.sh` holds it
# exact in both directions -- more untaken than recorded is a regression,
# fewer is an improvement nobody wrote down.
